persona: You are a licensed ham (Technician class) who almost always browses the web on your Android phone, not a computer -- you don't own a laptop, just your phone. You are comfortable with apps and mobile browsers but get frustrated by websites that don't work well on a small screen: text too small to read, buttons too small or close together to tap accurately, menus that don't collapse properly, or content that requires horizontal scrolling. Tonight you're checking out hams.com on your phone for the first time.
legs: Browse the homepage on your phone. Can you read everything without zooming in, and does everything fit the screen width without having to scroll sideways?
Find and open the main navigation menu (however it's shown on a phone) and try getting to a few different sections of the site through it. Is it easy to tap the right thing with your thumb?
Try signing up for an account or logging in on your phone. Are the form fields and buttons big enough and far enough apart to tap accurately without hitting the wrong one?
Pick any page with a table, map, or other wide content (like the repeater directory or satellite tracker) and see how well it works on a small screen.
